newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends week down on bearish data news.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends week down on bearish data news.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICALS
Sept (3rd pos) 1,190 rgt/tonne June (south) 1,227.50
Open/Hi/Low 1,193/1,203/1,187 Prev close 1,230
Prev settlement 1,194 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices closed week lower after news of bearish June crop estimates by Ivan Wong, and poor forecast on June 1-20 exports. News of active Chinese buying earlier this month helped to limit losses. Sept hit a resistance of 1,200 but fell back in late buying. Near-term seen at 1,180-1200.
PALM OIL PHYSICALS - Business reported in nearby CPOs, prices likely to stay rangebound next week.
Crop forecaster Ivan Wong, meanwhile, said Malaysia's palm oil output in June was expected to fall by 1.0 percent to 783,000 tonnes from May.
Wong put exports in June at 615,000 tonnes against the 626,606 tonnes in May.
He also estimated palm oil stocks for end-June at 770,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) forecast of 711,841 tonnes for end-May.
"Ivan's stock estimate was too high...it prompted players to throw their positions," another trader said.
Traders said there was some speculative buying when third month September futures hit the psychological level of 1,200.
Players were hesistant to trade actively, with the market watching closely the performance of refined products and consumer offtakes in near-term, said traders.
"India, for instance, is not buying actively because of its domestic low prices and poor demand," said one trader.
However, news that China was actively buying this month in the palm market helped to limit losses, the traders said.

"Yes, they have not been buying actively in recent months," said another trader, confirming the renewed Chinese interest. "They're coming back as current low prices against May is encouraging them to import more."
SGS said China's import of Malaysian palm oil was estimated at 94,300 tonnes for June 1-20 against the 43,100 tonnes in May 1-20.
In physicals, business was confined mainly to CPO months and prices could stay stagnant unless strong demand and bullish news appeared, said traders.
June (south) crude palm oil saw offers at 1,227.50 ringgit against bids at 1,222.50 after trading at 1,227.50.
June (central) saw offers at 1,215 versus 1,210 with earlier trades at 1,215 and 1,212.50.
July (south) was offered at 1,227.50 against bids of 1,222.50 and July (central) at 1,215 against bids of 1,210.
In refined products, July RBD palm oil was offered at $517.50 and Aug/Sept at $510.
July RBD palm olein saw offers at $560 and Aug/Sept at $555 and Oct/Nov/Dec at $555. Aug/Sept was traded at $555.
July RBD palm stearin was offered at $395, Aug/Sept at $390 and Aug palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $287.50.
THird month, September futures closed four ringgit down at 1,190 ringgit ($473.16) a tonne.
